scope: Initial read-only audit; no browser journey or complete semantic source audit has been performed.

findings.finding: The active public release is synthetic: four fictional candidacies, two fictional districts and twenty questions. No real 2023 programme positions have been released.

Object.entries(answerKeys) enumerates integer keys 0,1,2 before -2,-1. The rendered scale therefore starts neutral/agree/strongly agree, then strongly disagree/disagree. Use an explicit ordered array and test visible label/value order.
findings.verification: node --input-type=module; Object.entries on the exact answer key map

findings.finding: The isolated rent-cap example does not reproduce a global sign inversion: answer -2 versus supporting position +2 gives similarity 0; versus opposing position -2 gives similarity 1. Single-question partial overlaps are 0 for alpha/beta and 100 for gamma. This does not validate other mappings, the aggregate or the browser journey.
findings.verification: node --experimental-strip-types imports parseBank/similarity/match and the active hashed bank

findings.finding: Result details present every numerically answered question under cited agreements and differences. They show a party stance and the user label but no per-question match/difference/contribution. Users cannot readily distinguish a disagreement from the overall result. Explain both separately, never call every cited stance an agreement.

The existing literal compiler recognises exact synthetic Apoyamos/Rechazamos prefixes. It is not a semantic reading of real programmes. grounded_positions.py validates submitted ranges/schema; it does not prove the numeric interpretation. Real questions and mappings require documented agent reading and authored rationales.

Native extraction confirms downloaded PDFs have 112 pages (PP), 182 (Sumar), 76 (PACMA). Initial housing-page inspection is not a full analysis. PDF page index and printed page number differ, so retain both. No party value is inferred from this inspection.

nextChecks: Trace visible answer label through submitted value, stored answer, authored proposition direction, cited party position, weighted contribution and rendered explanation.
Independently validate every released 2023 mapping against the full source context; do not apply a blanket arithmetic sign reversal.
